soccer_events_to_frame(dataset: 'Any', *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Union[pl.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]' Turn a kloppy dataset (any provider, any file) into a tidy frame. The one place the package's column convention is applied to kloppy output: one row per event, columns snake-cased (kloppy's own names -- event_id, event_type, period_id, timestamp, team_id, player_id, coordinates_x, coordinates_y, ... -- already are, so this is a no-op guard for any extra column). Parameters Returns A polars DataFrame (pandas with return_as_pandas=True), one row per event. Coordinates are in the dataset's coordinate system -- kloppy's default is a 0-1 normalized pitch; pass coordinates="statsbomb" (etc.) to kloppy's loader to keep the provider's units. Raises Example from kloppy import statsbomb from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_events_to_frame ds = statsbomb.load(event_data="8658.json", lineup_data="lineups_8658.json") df = soccer_events_to_frame(ds) print(df.shape) # Useful parameter combination df_pd = soccer_events_to_frame(ds, return_as_pandas=True) # Pipeline next step (one line) df.filter(pl.col("event_type") == "SHOT").select("player_id", "coordinates_x", "coordinates_y")

soccer_open_dataset(provider: 'str', match_id: 'Union[int, str]', **kwargs: 'Any') -> 'Any' Load one match of a provider's free open event data as a kloppy EventDataset. provider="statsbomb" reads StatsBomb open data (https://github.com/statsbomb/open-data) through kloppy.statsbomb.load_open_data(match_id=...). That data is free for research and non-commercial use only, under StatsBomb's open-data license -- read it before publishing anything built on it. This is the input soccer_spadl expects; soccer_open_events is the same load flattened to a frame. Parameters Returns A kloppy EventDataset. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_open_dataset, soccer_spadl dataset = soccer_open_dataset("statsbomb", 8658) actions = soccer_spadl(dataset) # Pipeline next step (one line) frame = dataset.to_df(engine="polars")

soccer_open_events(provider: 'str', match_id: 'Union[int, str]', *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False, **kwargs: 'Any') -> 'Union[pl.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]' Load one match of a provider's free open event data as a tidy frame. provider="statsbomb" reads StatsBomb open data (https://github.com/statsbomb/open-data) through kloppy.statsbomb.load_open_data(match_id=...). That data is free for research and non-commercial use only, under StatsBomb's open-data license -- read it before publishing anything built on it. Other kloppy open samples (Metrica, SkillCorner) follow the same shape and are added on request. Parameters Returns A polars DataFrame (pandas with return_as_pandas=True), one row per event; see soccer_events_to_frame for the columns. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_open_events df = soccer_open_events("statsbomb", 8658) print(df.shape) # Useful parameter combination df_pd = soccer_open_events("statsbomb", 8658, coordinates="statsbomb", return_as_pandas=True) # Pipeline next step (one line) df.filter(pl.col("event_type") == "SHOT").group_by("team_id").len()

soccer_spadl(dataset: 'Any', *, game_id: 'Optional[Union[int, str]]' = None, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> "Union[pl.DataFrame, 'pd.DataFrame']" Convert a kloppy event dataset to SPADL actions on the 105 x 68 pitch. Every action attacks left to right (kloppy ACTION_EXECUTING_TEAM orientation), so a frame from any provider kloppy reads is comparable. StatsBomb is the tested path. Parameters Returns One row per on-ball action with the SPADL columns (type_name, result_name, bodypart_name, start/end coordinates in meters, time_seconds from the period's kick-off). Empty dataset -> zero-row frame with the same schema. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_open_dataset, soccer_spadl actions = soccer_spadl(soccer_open_dataset("statsbomb", 8658)) print(actions.shape) # Pipeline next step (one line) actions.filter(pl.col("type_name") == "shot").group_by("team_id").len()

soccer_xthreat_rate(actions: 'pl.DataFrame', model: 'Optional[XThreat]' = None, *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Union[pl.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]' Append xt_value (Expected Threat added by each successful pass, dribble or cross) to a SPADL frame. Parameters Returns actions with a Float64 xt_value column (null for actions xT does not value). Raises Example import polars as pl from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_open_dataset, soccer_spadl, soccer_xthreat_rate actions = soccer_xthreat_rate(soccer_spadl(soccer_open_dataset("statsbomb", 8658))) print(actions.group_by("player_id").agg(pl.col("xt_value").sum()).sort("xt_value", descending=True).head())

soccer_espn_reep_team_crosswalk(league: 'str | None' = None, *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' ESPN soccer team id -> reep team id, with reep's ids for the same club at about 20 providers. One row per ESPN team in the leagues the table covers: eng.1, eng.2, esp.1, ger.1, ita.1, fra.1, usa.1 and mex.1 (the clubs ESPN listed when the table was built, 2026-11-26). The table ships with sdv-py; no request is made. reep data is CC0 1.0 (release 2026.25). NWSL is not covered: reep has no row for 5 of its 16 clubs, below the 75% per-league floor. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per espn_team_id (unique). Every column is text (Utf8): espn_team_id joins espn_soccer_teams_site().team_id and the ESPN soccer scoreboard and summary team ids as it is. The reep columns are null when no reep row is that club (match_method == "unmatched"). Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_espn_reep_team_crosswalk xw = soccer_espn_reep_team_crosswalk() print(xw.shape) # One league, as pandas epl = soccer_espn_reep_team_crosswalk(league="eng.1", return_as_pandas=True) # Pipeline next step (one line) xw.select("espn_team_id", "key_transfermarkt", "key_fbref").drop_nulls("key_transfermarkt")

load_soccer_transfermarkt_clubs(*, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Load the CC0 Transfermarkt clubs table: one row per club of the first-tier leagues the dataset covers. About 800 clubs, each with its league, squad profile and stadium as of its last season in the dataset. A snapshot current to 2026-07-06 (not refreshed), read on every call from the release mirror. Licence: CC0 1.0. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per club_id (Int64), the id soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk maps ESPN teams to. A column holding a value of another type comes back as text with a SchemaDriftWarning. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_clubs clubs = load_soccer_transfermarkt_clubs() # ESPN Premier League teams with their Transfermarkt club rows from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk(league="eng.1").join(clubs, on="club_id", how="left")

load_soccer_transfermarkt_competitions(*, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Load the CC0 Transfermarkt competitions table: the leagues and cups the dataset covers. 65 competitions: first-tier domestic leagues, domestic cups and international club competitions, read on every call from the release mirror. Licence: CC0 1.0. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per competition_id (text, e.g. "GB1"), the id the clubs and players tables carry as domestic_competition_id / current_club_domestic_competition_id. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_competitions comps = load_soccer_transfermarkt_competitions() # First-tier leagues only import polars as pl comps.filter(pl.col("sub_type") == "first_tier")

load_soccer_transfermarkt_player_valuations(*, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Load the CC0 Transfermarkt market-value history: one row per player and valuation date. About 656,000 valuations, from 2000 to 2026-06-12 (the snapshot is not refreshed), read on every call from the release mirror. Licence: CC0 1.0. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per (player_id, date); player_id and current_club_id are Int64 and join the players and clubs tables. A column holding a value of another type comes back as text with a SchemaDriftWarning. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_player_valuations values = load_soccer_transfermarkt_player_valuations() # One player's value curve import polars as pl values.filter(pl.col("player_id") == 418560).sort("date")

load_soccer_transfermarkt_players(*, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Load the CC0 Transfermarkt players table: one row per player, with current club and market value. About 50,000 players: everyone who appeared for a club of the first-tier leagues the dataset covers (Premier League, LaLiga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, MLS, Liga MX and about 20 more). A snapshot current to 2026-07-06 (not refreshed), read on every call from the release mirror. Licence: CC0 1.0. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per player_id (Int64). current_club_id (Int64) joins club_id of load_soccer_transfermarkt_clubs and of soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk. A column holding a value of another type comes back as text with a SchemaDriftWarning. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_players players = load_soccer_transfermarkt_players() print(players.shape) # Most valuable players players.sort("market_value_in_eur", descending=True, nulls_last=True).head(10)

load_soccer_transfermarkt_transfers(*, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' Load the CC0 Transfermarkt transfers table: one row per player move between clubs, with its fee. About 175,000 transfers involving the clubs the dataset covers, to the 2025-26 season (the snapshot is current to 2026-07-06 and not refreshed), read on every call from the release mirror. Licence: CC0 1.0. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per transfer. player_id, from_club_id and to_club_id are Int64 Transfermarkt ids. A column holding a value of another type comes back as text with a SchemaDriftWarning. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_transfers moves = load_soccer_transfermarkt_transfers() # The largest fees of one season import polars as pl moves.filter(pl.col("transfer_season") == "25/26").sort("transfer_fee", descending=True, nulls_last=True)

soccer_espn_transfermarkt_player_crosswalk(league: 'str | None' = None, *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' ESPN soccer athlete id -> Transfermarkt player_id, for the first-tier leagues' current ESPN rosters. One row per athlete on the ESPN rosters (fetched 2026-11-27) of the eng.1, esp.1, ger.1, ita.1, fra.1, usa.1 and mex.1 teams whose Transfermarkt club is in the dataset: 4,346 athletes, 3,661 resolved (84%). The table ships with sdv-py; no request is made. An athlete is resolved by birth date and name against every Transfermarkt player: exactly one player with the same birth date and a shared name token, or, among several, the one with the athlete's citizenship. A 1 January birth date is too common a stand-in to count alone, so such an athlete is resolved only when exactly one same-date, same-name player also plays for the team's Transfermarkt club (or moved to it from 2025-07-01) or shares the citizenship. No player is matched to two athletes, and where the reep register carries both ids they agree on 99% of 2,478 pairs. Known limits: an ESPN birth date that belongs to a same-surname player resolves to that player (about a dozen athletes found at review), first names are not compared, and ESPN and Transfermarkt spell some countries differently ("USA", "Ivory Coast"), so the citizenship checks never fire for those athletes. The Transfermarkt data ends in July 2026, so a player who joined later can resolve with his previous club. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per espn_athlete_id (Utf8, unique). player_id (Int64) joins load_soccer_transfermarkt_players().player_id and load_soccer_transfermarkt_player_valuations(); it is null, with match_method == "unmatched", when no rule resolved the athlete. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_espn_transfermarkt_player_crosswalk xw = soccer_espn_transfermarkt_player_crosswalk() print(xw.shape) # One league, as pandas epl = soccer_espn_transfermarkt_player_crosswalk(league="eng.1", return_as_pandas=True) # Market values for ESPN athletes from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_players xw = soccer_espn_transfermarkt_player_crosswalk() xw.join(load_soccer_transfermarkt_players(), on="player_id").select("espn_athlete_id", "market_value_in_eur")

soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk(league: 'str | None' = None, *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'pl.DataFrame | pd.DataFrame' ESPN soccer team id -> Transfermarkt club_id, for the leagues of the ESPN <-> reep crosswalk. Read from the bundled ESPN <-> reep table (soccer_espn_reep_team_crosswalk), whose reep rows carry the Transfermarkt id, plus a reviewed id for a club whose reep row has none. No request is made. A newly promoted club can carry a club_id the Transfermarkt clubs table does not list: that snapshot ends in July 2026 and covers first tiers only. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per espn_team_id (Utf8, unique; joins the ESPN soccer frames' team ids). club_id is Int64, null when no Transfermarkt id is known, and never on two ESPN teams. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.soccer import soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk tm = soccer_espn_transfermarkt_team_crosswalk(league="eng.1") # Current Transfermarkt squads of the ESPN Premier League teams from sportsdataverse.soccer import load_soccer_transfermarkt_players tm.join(load_soccer_transfermarkt_players(), left_on="club_id", right_on="current_club_id")
